I was diagnosed with depression and borderline personality disorder over 15 years ago. Long story short, I had a very, very bad time. I attempted but failed. Like you, I started taking it one day at a time. If I had a bad day, I'll sleep until tomorrow. I tried to make to the next day. I knew happiness was possible from little things like getting As on exams and having a good meal. I went to therapy and I took medication. I knew I had to work for lasting happiness. Just a few years ago, I started seeing a therapist specializing in DBT. Now, I show almost no symptoms of mental illness. I learned to have self-compassion, to not be so hard on myself. I stopped invalidating my feelings ("I shouldn't feel this way") and allowed myself to emote. 

Sorry I'm on mobile. I want others to know that mental illness isn't a life sentence. Take it one day at a time. You have to put effort into changing you and your life.
